July 8th 2026

**CURRENT STATUS OF THE HUBS**

**Definition:** A **Hub** is a Jupyter notebook that provides the computational framework for integrating, executing, and demonstrating additional functionalities that extend the capabilities of the CESM simulator model. Each of the functionalities are motivated in the grant proposal submitted from Jingyi’s lab, with a LS from DSI, for NSF described here [https://uwmadison.box.com/s/2i0pffh5xc17yukzpqxztl4fru6n4rfx](https://uwmadison.box.com/s/2i0pffh5xc17yukzpqxztl4fru6n4rfx)

**Hub 1 \- Data Analysis**

* **Goal:** providing the user this layer to explore the data from NEON (native data for CESM)  
* **Input:** The current development calls the data from S3. In S3 there is a copy of [archive](https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1YOUqt_alGSc9at3cbW_3Vzq7MaeZXsFN?usp=share_link)5 NEON stations data, both input (NEON) and output (CESM output) of the CESM simulator for demonstration purposes.  
* **Expected Output:** Plots of data, histograms [https://github.com/UW-Madison-DSI/exsoil-nsf-prototype-refactor/blob/main/notebooks/Data\_Hub.ipynb](https://github.com/UW-Madison-DSI/exsoil-nsf-prototype-refactor/blob/main/notebooks/Data_Hub.ipynb)  
* **Status:** Completed

**Hub 2 \- Modeling Hub**

* **Goal:** The hub ingests CESM output (native output after processing NEON data) and demonstrates the capabilities described in this framework for applying the Kalman Filter. Specifically, the hub evaluates model fit and performs parameter adjustments using a Kalman Filter–based approach.  
* **Dependencies:** [https://github.com/UW-Madison-DSI/exsoil-nsf-prototype-refactor/tree/main/analytics\_modules](https://github.com/UW-Madison-DSI/exsoil-nsf-prototype-refactor/tree/main/analytics_modules)  
* **Input:** CESM simulations/outputs  
* **Expected Output: [https://github.com/UW-Madison-DSI/ctsm-nsf-demonstration/blob/main/notebooks/misfit\_eval.ipynb](https://github.com/UW-Madison-DSI/ctsm-nsf-demonstration/blob/main/notebooks/misfit_eval.ipynb)**  
* **Status:** Completed

**Hub 3 \- Experimentation Hub**

* **Goal:** The hub ingests NEON data into the CESM workflow, after specific scenarios of parameter perturbation or transformations. The hub is designed to demonstrate and compare how the CESM output when an input perturbation and when no perturbation of the input differ doing a t-test. This module touches the backend of CESM as it needs to process ”new” data e.g. NEON data under a transformation. It requires the output of CESM for data under perturbation and the output for data under no perturbation in order to generate 2 outputs to compare (please see diagram in page 4).  
* **Dependencies: [https://github.com/UW-Madison-DSI/exsoil-nsf-prototype-refactor/blob/main/cesm-tools/site\_and\_regional/run\_neon\_v2.py](https://github.com/UW-Madison-DSI/exsoil-nsf-prototype-refactor/blob/main/cesm-tools/site_and_regional/run_neon_v2.py)** Please consider that this module called v2 is a version 2 of the original wrapper “run\_neon.py”; there are many ways to perform this task, but working at the backend level of CESM involving working natively on the foltran-based source code was something I tried and may be difficult or require more SE expertise, so then I opt for the solution to work at the level of “run\_neon.py” original wrapper instead, creating this run\_neon\_v2.py and locating it in the same site as run\_neon.py via Docker file (lines 32-34) [https://github.com/UW-Madison-DSI/exsoil-nsf-prototype-refactor/blob/main/Dockerfile](https://github.com/UW-Madison-DSI/exsoil-nsf-prototype-refactor/blob/main/Dockerfile) makes sense to me for easy integration carrying the underlying dependencies  
* **Input:** CESM simulations/outputs after transforming: PFT, Soil type and \[\]  
* **Expected Output:**   
* **Status:** Completed

**Notes:** 

- Hub 2 has as a backend of the framework here [https://github.com/UW-Madison-DSI/exsoil-nsf-prototype-refactor/tree/main/analytics\_modules](https://github.com/UW-Madison-DSI/exsoil-nsf-prototype-refactor/tree/main/analytics_modules)  
- Hub 2 and 3 have not been tested against the new architecture/design that pulls native data from NEON  
- The rationale for incorporating S3 into the architecture is two fold: (1) it provides an immutable source of data that can be used as a reference for comparison after perturbations are introduced, and (2) it improves efficiency by reducing the need to repeatedly download data from NEON during the workflow.  
- No solution is inherently wrong; the new design reflects different considerations, preferences, and an evaluation of long-term maintenance and feasibility. Please view what I implemented as a resource that can be leveraged when useful, taking the aspects that provide the most value for the current and future needs.

**Maria’s suggestion:**

- There is an opportunity between the existing hubs and the current architecture Steve and Abe worked on, that means integrating hubs into the new design and pointing out to the data sources as in such new design OR viceversa, adjusting the design to the functionalities of the hubs e.g. maintaining the S3 source etc. My suggestion is going in the first way to take the most of the current design from Steve and Abe.  
- I think that the easy way to go is simply adapting one jupyter notebook at a time, starting from the “Data Analysis” one that is the simplest and mapping out what needs to be changed to match the architecture design and reaching out to Jingyi to test out such portions.

# **MVP**

Goal \- the goal is to extend the capacities of the [https://ncar.github.io/ncar-neon-books/quick\_start\_docker\_part2.html](https://ncar.github.io/ncar-neon-books/quick_start_docker_part2.html) CTSM model in three main aspects:

1. Data Access: we have put together NEON weather data in UW-Madison S3 to feed the workflow.  
2. Model Evaluation: refers to an [statistical framework](https://github.com/UW-Madison-DSI/exsoil-nsf-prototype-refactor/tree/main/analytics_modules) incorporated in the backend for 1\) model evaluation eg goodness of fit, bias, etc, 2\) data assimilation: kalman filter of the CESM physics model  
3. Scenario Analysis: allowing in the workflow the option to change data by transformations and compare the simulator on such data vs the simulation with no data change. The variables to incorporate are: PFT, Soil type, pcpt. This part is the most challenging and refers to the main python script: run\_neon\_v2.py [here](https://github.com/UW-Madison-DSI/exsoil-nsf-prototype-refactor/blob/main/cesm-tools/site_and_regional/run_neon_v2.py)

Quick start:

1. On the current tool please see  
   1. Dockerfile [https://github.com/UW-Madison-DSI/exsoil-nsf-prototype-refactor/blob/main/Dockerfile](https://github.com/UW-Madison-DSI/exsoil-nsf-prototype-refactor/blob/main/Dockerfile)  
   2. For the frontend design please check the jupyter notebooks (at this point there is **no** need for a security access layer such as user-password)  
2. Or please check the documentation of the original tool that we are extending [https://ncar.github.io/ncar-neon-books/quick\_start\_docker\_part2.html](https://ncar.github.io/ncar-neon-books/quick_start_docker_part2.html)

To be complete:

  - Task (the data access): data is now stored in s3 with uw madison network restriction. This is a configuration of the s3 bucket that Jingyi owns. For the tool to be usable elsewhere, this condition must be changed.  
  - Task (slowness of the tool): basic assessment.  
- Usability of the jupyter notebooks
